answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Lock. Each identity’s action history is hashed into a per-epoch fingerprint; a new epoch only accepts identities whose fingerprint evolves through bounded, continuous drift. Sudden replication of a lotus-like cluster of clones causes drift to exceed the lagoon-stable threshold, so the whole cohort is frozen and must re-earn continuity from scratch. An attacker therefore pays one full epoch of genuine, low-volume activity per identity—saffron-priced time and gas—before any clone can act at scale, making mass duplication linear in real elapsed work rather than in capital.
